first_attempt.cleanup_stderr: ForeignKeyViolation: update or delete on table "model_versions" violates foreign key constraint "drift_checks_model_version_id_fkey" on table "drift_checks" (Key (id)=(61ec5eef-0615-4505-848a-055ae167eda5) is still referenced from table "drift_checks").
first_attempt.finding: The cleanup script's own deletion order was incomplete: it missed drift_checks/drift_feature_results, and a second attempt also missed raw_records/data_quality_checks (both reference dataset_version_id) and pipeline_runs (also references dataset_version_id, blocking dataset_versions deletion) -- each attempt ran as a single uncommitted transaction, so a mid-transaction FK error rolled back the ENTIRE attempt's deletes, not just the failing statement. This is itself a small, honestly-reported instance of the same 'onboarding/teardown is not fully tooled' finding as Step 1: removing a model correctly requires knowing the full FK dependency graph across 9 tables, which is not documented anywhere either.

second_attempt_corrected_order.elapsed_note: Not separately timed; run manually after diagnosing the FK order via the actual Postgres error messages (see first_attempt). Full corrected order: drift_feature_results -> drift_checks -> production_predictions/evaluation_results/deployment_events/alerts(by version) -> pipeline_stages/sla_violations/alerts(by run) -> data_quality_checks/raw_records(by dataset_version) -> model_versions -> pipeline_runs -> dataset_versions -> audit_logs -> the model row itself, committed once at the end.
